Take one lattice spacing as \(1\) unit.

- Quadrilateral I has side lengths \(1,\sqrt2,1,\sqrt2\), so
  \[
  P_{\text{I}}=2+2\sqrt2.
  \]
  Its area is \(1\) square unit.

- Quadrilateral II has side lengths \(\sqrt5,\sqrt2,1,\sqrt2\), so
  \[
  P_{\text{II}}=1+2\sqrt2+\sqrt5.
  \]
  Using its lattice coordinates and the shoelace formula also gives area \(1\) square unit.

Thus the areas are equal, while
\[
P_{\text{II}}-P_{\text{I}}
=(1+2\sqrt2+\sqrt5)-(2+2\sqrt2)
=\sqrt5-1>0.
\]
So the perimeter of I is less than the perimeter of II.

\[
\boxed{\text{E: The quadrilaterals have the same area, but the perimeter of I is less than the perimeter of II.}}
\]
